Every statement is at least as general as the paper's sentence, or narrower only where the REPORT discloses it and keeps the row partial. The build, the sorry count and the axioms are as claimed. The fix is a rewording of four docstring bullets, which the master can make at graduation; no new closer round is needed.

labels.label: lem:J_int
labels.notes: J_int states ETT.tex:1801-1804 exactly as printed, Int J^±(p) ∩ Z^∓(M) = I^±(p) for both signs at every p. Its hypotheses are DEC-25's [SingularGXStructure (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) M] and the OQ-18 reading of the causality: absolutely minimal, with IsoChartsCoverDEC25 over massAModelCausality, i.e. E₀ and E_κ for κ > 0. There is no strong causality, connectedness, T2 or second countability; T1 comes from SFABTZ.t1Space_of_isoChartsCover. No hidden hypothesis. The file has three more theorems for this label. interior_Jplus_diff_sing and interior_Jminus_eq rewrite J_int through Zminus_eq and Zplus_eq, and J_int_sing pairs them. They are new at M: SFALocal, SFABTZ and SFALine have no J_int. They are thin instantiations of Causality.J_int (PushUp.lean:192). One side remark: interior_Jplus_diff_sing is DEC-64's repair I⁺(p) = Int J⁺(p) ∖ sing₀, which at the model is E0.Iplus_axis_eq_interior_diff. Here it holds at every point of every E≥0-manifold, which the master may cross-reference on the defi:causal_E0 row. Non-vacuous: nonvacuous_e0 (axis points) and nonvacuous_epi derive these conclusions from the file's theorems. The label is cited unmarked in the header (l.9), but l.45 writes it as **`lem:J_int`**, which ledger.py reads as a mark (finding 1).

labels.label: lem:cup_cap_sing
labels.notes: cup_cap_sing states ETT.tex:1813-1817, both signs, for every p and every sequence u → p. Its hypotheses are [T2Space M], hmin, hC and C.GloballyHyperbolic, the library's def:globally_hyperbolic. T2 is part of « singular flat spacetime » through topological spacetime (ETT.tex:254), and GH is the paper's own hypothesis, so nothing is added. No connectedness and no second countability. The one-sign forms, Iminus_eq_interior_iUnion_iInter and Iplus_eq_interior_iUnion_iInter, ask only hmin, hC and J^∓(x) closed for every x. They need no T2, no causality and no GH. All three are new at M (no SFALocal, SFABTZ or SFALine counterpart) and are thin instantiations of the Causality cores (PushUp.lean:214). Non-vacuous at E₀ for every sequence converging to an axis point (nonvacuous_e0, E0.globallyHyperbolic), at every point with the natural causality (nonvacuous_e0_natural), and at E_π (nonvacuous_epi). l.48 writes **`lem:cup_cap_sing`**, which is read as a mark (finding 1).

labels.label: rem:tarentin_exemples
labels.notes: tarentin proves the E≥0 sentence, ETT.tex:689-690, as C.Tarentin from hC alone. It uses no absolute minimality, separation or countability, so it is weaker than the paper's hypotheses. It is a verbatim alias of SFALocal.tarentin, which the rem:sing_tarentin row already curates. tarentin_exemples_local is an assembly with the same shape as the strict Causal.tarentin_exemples (Tarentin.lean:339). Its third conjunct replaces C.SingularFlatAxioms sing with IsoChartsCoverDEC25. The Minkowski, E_α and Misner conjuncts are reused, and the Misner one keeps the added hypothesis already curated. The row stays partial because the library has no Lorentzian manifolds. Non-vacuous at E₀ and E_π. l.51 writes **`rem:tarentin_exemples`**, which is read as a mark (finding 1).

labels.label: rem:lorentz_tarentin
labels.notes: compl_Zminus_eq gives C.Zminusᶜ = SFALocal.sing M 0 under hmin and hC, which is ETT.tex:785-787 with « BTZ points » read as sing₀(M). Zplus_eq gives C.Zplus = univ from hC alone (no minimality). lorentz_tarentin_local assembles them with minkowski_Z_eq_univ, in place of SingularFlatAxioms.Z_eq. All three are wrappers: Zplus_eq is the set form of SFALocal.mem_Zplus, Zminus_eq of SFALocal.mem_Zminus_iff, and compl_Zminus_eq is the complement of SFALocal.btz_pas_tarentin's second half. There is no hidden hypothesis, and minimality enters only through the BTZ half (kb/0135). Non-vacuous at E₀ (Z⁻ᶜ = axis) and at E_π (Z⁻ = E_π). l.53 writes **`rem:lorentz_tarentin`**, which is read as a mark (finding 1).

labels.label: rem:pas_plat
labels.notes: (ii) is ETT.tex:294. Its « I⁻(p) = ∅ » is Iminus_eq_empty, at every BTZ point under hmin and hC: as printed, with no causality and no T2. It is an alias of SFALocal.Iminus_eq_empty with the binders reordered. « J⁻(p) is the singular half-line below p » is btz_past, which adds T2 (DEC-25's manifold) and C.IsCausal. The causal hypothesis narrows the sentence, and that is disclosed: checklist l.78, SCOPE l.88, REPORT 'strengthened', row partial, and the curated l.294 finding on defi:causal_E0. So it is acceptable. btz_past is a thin assembly of SFALine.Jminus_eq_image and Iminus_eq_empty. Its conclusion matches the sentence: γ is a closed embedding and a future-directed causal curve (Inextensible ⊤ univ), with range the component of sing₀(M) through p, so γ(Iic 0) is the closed half-line ending at p. btz_past_bounds is new and small: the two inclusions of Jminus_eq_image's proof, without causality. Jminus_subset_sing is the set form of SFABTZ.mem_sing_zero_of_le. interior_Jminus_eq_empty and btz_causallyPlain_past are the M-level copies of the strict SingularFlatAxioms.interior_Jminus_eq_empty and btz_causallyPlain_past; they are new at M and need no T2. causallyPlain is a verbatim alias of SFALocal.causallyPlain. pas_plat_ii assembles all of these under T2, which its I⁻ and plainness conjuncts do not need; the separate theorems are there. rows_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 takes MassACovered M with IsAtlasCausalityDEC25 (the natural causality) and is non-vacuous at E₀ (nonvacuous_e0_natural). Not marked: l.55 writes **`rem:pas_plat` (ii)**, which the ledger regex does not match.

findings.what: True in the readings. SFALocal.causallyPlain gives C.CausallyPlain, both orientations, every open U and every A, at every E≥0-manifold whose causality is absolutely minimal with an isomorphic chart at each point; the natural causality is one such (SFALocal.of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25). It is witnessed with BTZ points at E₀ (nonvacuous_e0). The singular family of l.290 is the E≥0-manifolds: the abstract, l.127-128, has « the singular flat spacetimes carrying massive particles and BTZ lines ». So « it fails in the two families » is false as printed for that family. The finding is a refinement, not new. It strengthens the curated rem:pas_plat finding 1, whose last sentence reads « Nothing in the paper shows an E≥0-manifold is not causally plain (cf. OQ-16), so 'it fails in the two families' (l.290) is supported for (i) only. », from absence of evidence to refutation in the readings. Its Lean content is already curated on the rem:sing_tarentin row, in T-ett-sfa-local's note « Beyond the row: every such causality that is absolutely minimal is causally plain (causallyPlain; evidence for OQ-16 at every E≥0-manifold, not an answer) ». It is not yet on the rem:pas_plat row, whose note stops at T-ett-sfa-local-e0's « the E_κ charts are not covered ». The REPORT has four defects. (a) It misquotes the row: « The curated row says (ii) is « supported for (i) only » » should read « says 'it fails in the two families' (l.290) is supported for (i) only ». (b) Its suggested wording, « at singularities only its relational form is at stake », is wrong: the relational push-up also holds at every E≥0-manifold (SFALocal.pushUp, cor:pushup_sing; the row's curated finding 2). (c) The same claim is printed twice more and is not curated anywhere: in the abstract, l.131-132 (« Push-up is the silent hypothesis of classical causal theory, and it fails in both families of spacetimes we wish to cover »), and in the introduction, l.214-216 (« it fails again, in degenerate form, at the BTZ points of a singular flat spacetime »). (d) « the singular family » should be named as the E≥0-manifolds.

findings.where: REPORT.json, rem:pas_plat, findings[0] (dispatch finding 2, l.294) and its hypothesis note
findings.what: The by-hand sketch is correct; I checked the argument. If the component of sing₀(M) through p is compact, the development γ is periodic, so γ(]-∞,0]) is the whole component and btz_past_bounds gives equality. If it is not compact, γ is injective, since a development that returns to a point is periodic. It is then a homeomorphism onto the component, because locally it is the inverse chart r ↦ e⁻¹(r,0). If q ≤ p, the causal curve from q to p (causal arc-connectedness, from absolute minimality) lies in J⁻(p), hence in the component (SFABTZ.Jminus_subset_component). In each chart into E₀ the ball's relation on the axis is the τ-order (SFABTZ.le_ballOpens_iff), so γ⁻¹ of the curve does not decrease, and q ∈ γ(]-∞,0]). The finding is a refinement, not a duplicate. The compact case is already in the strict SFALine SCOPE (« on the circle the set equation J⁻(p) = γ(]−∞, 0]) would still hold (γ periodic, so J⁻(p) is the whole component), but γ is no closed embedding there, and J⁻(p) is no half-line ») and in the defi:causal_E0 note (« Causality is what makes γ(]−∞, 0]) a half-line »). The non-compact, non-causal case is the new part. It contradicts no curated text, but it shows that the curated l.294 finding on defi:causal_E0 says too much in « At M it holds when M is causal (…) and fails otherwise »: at a non-causal M the half-line fails only at BTZ points whose component is compact. The REPORT's hypothesis note and proposed blocked_on say the same too strongly (« The sentence is false as printed at non-causal M », « the half-line is false as printed at non-causal M »).
findings.fix: Record the finding as a note on rem:pas_plat, by hand, and do not make it a new paper_finding. In the curated defi:causal_E0 finding, replace « and fails otherwise. » with « and can fail otherwise, but only at a BTZ point whose component of sing₀(M) is compact: there γ is periodic and J⁻(p) = γ(]−∞, 0]) is the whole circle (by hand; with a non-compact component the set equation and the half-line hold with no causality, by hand, not formalized). ». Write « can fail at a non-causal M » wherever this audit's curation text describes the half-line.

answers.duplicates: None of the 25 theorems duplicates a strict theorem under the same name. The verbatim aliases of SFALocal, SFABTZ and SFALine are: tarentin = SFALocal.tarentin; causallyPlain = SFALocal.causallyPlain; Iminus_eq_empty = SFALocal.Iminus_eq_empty with reordered binders; Zplus_eq, the set form of SFALocal.mem_Zplus; Zminus_eq, the set form of SFALocal.mem_Zminus_iff; compl_Zminus_eq, the complement form of SFALocal.btz_pas_tarentin.2; Jminus_subset_sing, the set form of SFABTZ.mem_sing_zero_of_le. btz_past is a thin assembly of SFALine.Jminus_eq_image and Iminus_eq_empty. New at M, as instantiations of the abstract cores: J_int, interior_Jplus_diff_sing, interior_Jminus_eq, J_int_sing, Iminus_eq_interior_iUnion_iInter, Iplus_eq_interior_iUnion_iInter and cup_cap_sing. New at M, as copies of the strict SingularFlatAxioms proofs: interior_Jminus_eq_empty and btz_causallyPlain_past. btz_past_bounds is new. The assemblies are tarentin_exemples_local, lorentz_tarentin_local, pas_plat_ii and rows_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25. Overlap with the sibling: through SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms (T2, second countable), the strict SingularFlatAxioms.btz_past, interior_Jminus_eq_empty, Z_eq and the field tarentin also reach every Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold. This file's forms need less: no second countability, and no T2 except for the half-line and cup-cap. They complement the sibling rather than duplicate it.

rem:pas_plat.notes_append: (ii) at every E≥0-manifold, with no SingularFlatAxioms. I⁻(p) = ∅ at every BTZ point, M causal or not, with no Hausdorff (SingularRowsLocal.Iminus_eq_empty = SFALocal.Iminus_eq_empty; it uses absolute minimality, kb/0135). At every causal Hausdorff one, J⁻(p) = γ(]−∞, 0]), where γ is the BTZ line through p, a closed embedding onto the component of sing₀(M) through p (btz_past, from SFALine.Jminus_eq_image). With no causality, γ(]−∞, 0]) ⊆ J⁻(p) ⊆ range γ (btz_past_bounds). By hand, not formalized, the set equation holds with no causality too: on a compact component γ is periodic and both sides are the whole circle, and on a non-compact one γ is a homeomorphism onto the component and the chart time cannot decrease along a causal curve inside it. So what can fail at a non-causal M is « half-line », and only on a compact component. The row's finding holds at M: Int J⁻_U(A) = ∅ for every open U and every A ⊆ sing₀(M) (interior_Jminus_eq_empty, btz_causallyPlain_past), and M is causally plain (causallyPlain = SFALocal.causallyPlain, already curated on rem:sing_tarentin, T-ett-sfa-local), mixed E≥0-manifolds included. pas_plat_ii assembles these. Not vacuous at E₀ at every axis point, where γ is onto the whole axis (nonvacuous_e0, nonvacuous_e0_natural). Unmarked: (i) is not built; readings OQ-18, OQ-34, OQ-35, OQ-82; the half-line needs M causal.
rem:pas_plat.paper_findings_replace: In finding 1, replace « Nothing in the paper shows an E≥0-manifold is not causally plain (cf. OQ-16), so 'it fails in the two families' (l.290) is supported for (i) only. » with: « In the readings DEC-25, OQ-18, OQ-34/OQ-35 and OQ-82, every E≥0-manifold is causally plain. Its causality is absolutely minimal with an isomorphic chart at each point, the natural one included (Causal.SFALocal.causallyPlain, Causal.SingularRowsLocal.causallyPlain; witnessed with BTZ points at E₀), and it has the relational push-up (SFALocal.pushUp, cor:pushup_sing). The claim 'it fails in the two families' (l.290) is therefore refuted for the E≥0-manifolds, the singular family of the abstract (l.127–128), and holds for (i) only. The same applies to the abstract, 'it fails in both families of spacetimes we wish to cover' (l.131–132, with 'at a BTZ point, I^-(p) is empty while J^-(p) is not', l.134), and to the introduction, 'it fails again, in degenerate form, at the BTZ points of a singular flat spacetime' (l.214–216). What remains at a BTZ point is the pointwise defect I^-(p) = ∅ ≠ J^-(p) ∖ {p}, which causal plainness does not see because J^-(p) has empty interior. This is evidence for OQ-16, not a ruling. Suggested wording for l.290: 'This is the topological form of push-up. It fails in low regularity; at the BTZ points of an E≥0-manifold a degenerate relative of the defect appears, which causal plainness does not detect:', and the abstract and the introduction accordingly. »
